# MSFT research brief: % change from the 2026-08-07 close to the 2026-09-06 close

**Short version:** MSFT closed at 499.99 on 2026-08-07, after rising about 28% in two weeks on strong fiscal Q4 earnings and lower capex guidance. 2026-09-06 is a Sunday, so the question will use the 2026-09-04 close. Before then come CPI, Nvidia earnings and the Jackson Hole meeting. I found no prediction market or analyst view that maps cleanly onto this question.

Several search results returned pages dated after 2026-08-09. I ignored all of them, as instructed.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-08-07: The latest close is **499.99**, taken from your code's Yahoo Finance data. My fetches were blocked by the proxy, so I could not open Yahoo or stockanalysis.com myself to confirm it.
- The resolution date, 2026-09-06, is a Sunday, and Monday 2026-09-07 is Labor Day. That means the **Friday 2026-09-04 close** will decide the question. Counting trading days, that is about 20 sessions ahead, while your baseline assumed 21.
- Your baseline's percentiles, converted to % change from 499.99: p5 -12.5%, p10 -9.1%, p25 -4.3%, p50 -0.3%, p75 +4.3%, p90 +8.3%, p95 +12.4%.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has happened yet that settles the question. The stock has run up very sharply going into the window, as detailed in sections 3 and 4.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-07: The Toronto-listed MSFT receipt (TSX:MSFT) closed at 34.98, up about 7.5% from its 2026-07-31 close of 32.54. That roughly matches the US move. [stockanalysis TSX](https://stockanalysis.com/quote/tsx/MSFT/history/)
- 2026-08-03: MSFT closed at 487.76, up 4.96% on the day. That implies a 2026-07-31 close of about 464.7. Getting to 499.99 on 08-07 means a gain of about 7.6% in the week of Aug 3-7. [stockanalysis](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/msft/)
- 2026-08-02/03: The Motley Fool reported the shares rose nearly 22% in the week after earnings. [Fool](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/02/why-microsoft-stock-is-surging/)
- 2026-07-30: The stock jumped more than 14% at the open. Before the open it was quoted up about 8% at $420.02, which implies a prior close of about $389. [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/microsoft-beats-on-profit-and-revenue-shares-rise-after-hours-4821565)
- 2026-07-29: Microsoft reported fiscal Q4 2026 results:
  - Revenue was about $90.0B, up 18%, against a ~$87.6B estimate.
  - Adjusted EPS was $4.74 against a $4.24 estimate.
  - Azure grew about 41-43%; sources disagree on the exact figure.
  - Guidance for the current quarter calls for about 45% Azure growth, above estimates.
  - Calendar-2026 capex guidance fell to about $175B from about $190B. Microsoft says the two figures are comparable once a change in assumed data center lifespans is accounted for. Investors had feared FY27 capex near $220B.
  - Sources: [AA](https://aa.com.tr/en/science-technology/microsoft-beats-quarterly-revenue-estimates-as-azure-growth-accelerates/4013210), [Constellation](https://www.constellationr.com/insights/news/microsoft-azure-q4-revenue-surges-41-tops-100-billion-annual-revenue), [KuCoin](https://www.kucoin.com/blog/microsoft-q4-earnings-azure-growth-hits-43-percent-as-annual-cloud-revenue-tops-100-billion)
- 2026-07-23: Previews framed the report around capex and Azure. [S&P Global](https://www.spglobal.com/market-intelligence/en/news-insights/research/2026/07/microsoft-and-meta-earnings-previews), [Pepperstone](https://pepperstone.com/en-ae/insights/market-analysis/equities/microsoft-q4-fy2026-earnings-preview-ai-spending-free-cash-flow-guidance-and-the-key-levels-that-could-move-msft)
- Late April / May 2026 analyst price targets, all set before the rally:
  - Morgan Stanley $625
  - Goldman Sachs $610
  - Cantor Fitzgerald $608
  - Jefferies $575
  - Benchmark $525
  - BofA $515
  - Rothschild Redburn $440 (Neutral)
  - Sources: [TipRanks](https://www.tipranks.com/news/the-fly/morgan-stanley-ups-microsoft-target-elevates-to-top-pick-in-software-thefly), [Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/microsoft-corp-msft-price-target-143459021.html)

## 4. Base rates
- Your code's 3-year empirical distribution for 21-session returns has a median of about 0%. The 25-75% range is about ±4.3%, and the 5-95% range runs from about -12.5% to +12.4%.
- MSFT's recent volatility is well above that baseline. It gained about 22% in one week and then about 7.6% the next, so roughly +28% in two weeks. Moves on that scale usually come with higher implied volatility, so the tails may be wider than the historical baseline suggests. I could not find current options-implied volatility.
- I could not find specific studies on how mega-caps perform in the month after a post-earnings gap of more than 20%.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Polymarket lists "MSFT above ___ in August 2026" contracts that settle on the last trading day of August. That is a different date from this question's 09-04 close, and one mirror site flagged the related markets as illiquid. I could not retrieve prices as of 08-09 or earlier. [Polymarket](https://polymarket.com/event/msft-above-in-august-2026)
- I found no Kalshi or Manifold market on MSFT for this window.
- The analyst targets listed above predate the rally. I found no target changes after earnings that were dated on or before 2026-08-09.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Around 2026-08-12/13: US CPI and PPI for July (my estimate; the exact release dates are not confirmed).
- 2026-08-26, after the close: Nvidia's fiscal Q2 2027 earnings, a key read-across for AI and capex sentiment (confirmed). [Wall Street Horizon](https://www.wallstreethorizon.com/nvidia-earnings-calendar)
- 2026-08-27 to 08-29: the Jackson Hole symposium, with the Fed Chair's keynote expected 08-28. [Regards of Wall Street](https://www.regardsofwallstreet.com/news/stock-market-week-ahead-august-24-2026)
- 2026-09-04: the August jobs report, released the same day as the deciding close.
- Microsoft-specific risks with no set date: news on the OpenAI or Anthropic relationships, AI capex commentary from peers, and Copilot adoption numbers (30M+ paid seats were cited at earnings).
